result.title: Depth Memory
result.summary: Residual connections propagate information through a network by additively accumulating layer outputs. Recently proposed alternatives, such as Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections (mHC) and Attention Residuals (AttnRes), instead use more expressive depth aggregation mechanisms that improve language modeling performance at scale. In this work, we consider the mixing of representations over depth as a problem of storing and retrieving information across layers. Formalizing this perspective, we introduce Depth Memory (DM), a unified framework that describes the standard pre-layer-norm (PreLN) transformer, mHC, and AttnRes in terms of streams that carry representations through the network. One such stream, for example, could be an explicit memory stream that is queried to enrich the input to every layer, and whose output is subsequently written back into the memory for use by later layers. For AttnRes, this memory stream is a growing cache of explicit layer representations. For mHC, it is an expanded residual stream. Building on this view, we propose Linear Depth Memory (LDM), which formulates information retrieval across depth as a regression problem solved using recursive least squares. The resulting architecture propagates three streams across depth: the standard residual stream, a linear associative memory stream, and an inverse covariance stream. For high-throughput training and inference, we propose a hardware-aware implementation of LDM that reduces peak activation memory and memory traffic. LDM consistently achieves the lowest perplexities among PreLN, mHC and AttnRes baselines at the 400M and 1.5B parameter scales, alongside competitive zero-shot accuracy.

AI.brief_summary: 论文把 Transformer 的跨深度表示混合视为「跨层存储与检索」，用一个统一框架刻画 PreLN、mHC 与 AttnRes 中的表示流，并提出以递归最小二乘求解深度检索的 Linear Depth Memory（LDM）及配套硬件感知实现，在 400M/1.5B 语言建模上取得更低困惑度。
AI.relevance_reason: 纯文本语言建模工作，但其「记忆流被查询以丰富每层输入、输出再写回」的视角，以及 AttnRes 对逐层表示缓存的注意力式聚合，可能为 LVR 的推理状态更新、深度与缓存对 latent 相似度的影响提供可供核查的方法线索。
